Byomkesh.description: The protagonist, a 'truth-seeker' or detective known for his keen observation and logical reasoning.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates the story and assists in investigations.

Baikuntha Das.description: A miserly goldsmith and jeweller, whose mysterious murder is the central case of the chapter.

Bhanupratap Singh.description: A constable who assists in the capture of Shailen-babu.

Munger.description: A historic town in Bihar, India, known for its fort and as the setting for this chapter.

Bihar.description: A state in eastern India where the events of the story take place.

Calcutta.description: Now Kolkata, a major city in eastern India, home to Byomkesh and Ajit.

Ganga.description: The Ganges River, a major and sacred river in India, flowing near Munger.

Mir Kasim.description: An 18th-century Nawab of Bengal, historically associated with Munger's fort.

Nabadwip.description: A town in West Bengal, India, mentioned as the home of Baikuntha-babu's relatives and the site of his daughter's wedding.

Jessore.description: A town (now in Bangladesh), mentioned as the origin of Baikuntha-babu's son-in-law.

Gaya.description: A city in Bihar, India, considered holy for performing Hindu last rites.

Balloonbazar.description: A Bengali-dominated locality in Munger where Tarashankar-babu resides.

Kashtaharini Ghat.description: A riverside ghat (steps leading to the river) in Munger, visited by the characters.

Peer Shanfa.description: A tomb or shrine in Munger, referenced as a local landmark.

Robert Clive.description: A British colonial figure, referenced in the context of Munger's history.

Jarasandha.description: A legendary king from Indian epic history, referenced in connection with Munger's ancient past.

babu.description: ‘Babu’ is a respectful suffix or title for men, often used in Bengal and northern India; in this story, it is attached to several characters’ names as an honorific.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and other ingredients, chewed for its stimulant effects.

dhoti.description: A traditional men's garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs, commonly worn in India.

sari.description: A traditional garment worn by women in India, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

hookah.description: A water pipe used for smoking, popular in India and the Middle East.

planchette.description: A small board supported on casters, used in séances to communicate with spirits by spelling out messages.

zamindar.description: A landowner, especially one who collected taxes from peasants under the former system in India.

phaeton.description: A type of horse-drawn carriage, referenced here as a mode of transport.
